arguments.heading: What happened at the argument
paragraphs: Mr. Jett argued the government must disprove duress beyond a reasonable doubt.
Mr. Gornstein argued the defendant must prove duress because it is an affirmative defense.
Justice Souter questioned whether the defendant freely chooses to commit the crime.
Justice Souter asked what the added element of the defense is.

paragraphs: the side that brought the case wants the government to disprove duress beyond a reasonable doubt.

sections.heading: What each side says
paragraphs: the side that brought the case argues duress is an affirmative defense that excuses criminal conduct.
The government argues the defendant must prove the defense because it excuses serious conduct.
